It cannot exist prior to motion (that would be circular), nor in the going or gone (v.12 showed this). V.12 asked WHERE the beginning is; v.13 asks whether the CONCEPT of beginning can be coherently established prior to motion. Siderits/Katsura: the verse applies a second-order analysis — not just examining motion but examining the examination.","quantum":"CPT Symmetry / Time-Reversal Invariance: Fundamental quantum equations are time-symmetric — they work identically forwards and backwards. Ultimately, cessation of motion faces the same analytical problems as its beginning — it cannot be inherently located.","commonMisconception":"Not denying that things stop moving.
